title: Noor and the Harvest
premise: Ivo Reyes, a hospice nurse who hears the dying count backwards toward something, has kept the village of Hollowmere safe for years by counting doors, lights, and names. When a church bell that was melted down in 1911 begins to ring at dusk, the village's carefully buried covenant with the founders' ritual starts to unravel, and Ivo learns the hospice patients were never dying naturally — they were being harvested to feed the thing the founders bound. With the last of the old families refusing to finish the ritual, Ivo and a found family of the village's invisible people must choose: complete the harvest and survive, or break the covenant and face what was bound. In the end, Ivo takes the founders' place inside the bell's silence, trading their own name into the count so the village — and the people they love — can finally stop counting.
about_author: Casper Okonkwo is the pen name of a former night-shift caregiver who writes horror about the quiet violence of institutions and the families people build in their gaps. They live somewhere with too many doors and count them anyway.

chapters.title: The Counting Hours
chapters.summary: Ivo Reyes, POV. A night at Hollowmere hospice: Ivo hears Mrs. Adeyemi counting backwards from forty, keeps the hallway lights on, and counts the doors twice. The emotional beat is weary tenderness — Ivo's rituals are love disguised as compulsion, and the reader learns the counting is how the dying signal something is coming for them.

chapters.title: A Bell That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. At dusk the village hears a church bell ring, though St. Alder's bell was melted down in 1911 and the tower is a roofless shell. The villagers pretend not to hear. The beat is dread under politeness — Ivo realizes everyone in Hollowmere has been pretending together for a very long time.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV, searching the hospice attic for records, finds the founders' ledger: names in columns, dates of death, and a tally that matches the backwards counts exactly. The beat is vertigo — the hospice isn't a hospice; it's the last functioning part of the ritual, and Ivo has been its unwitting hand.

chapters.title: People Made of Margins
chapters.summary: Multi-POV chapter introducing Ivo's found family: Tam, the undocumented gardener who hears the bell in his sleep; Sister Brigid, a defrocked nun; and Odile, the teenage girl nobody claims. The beat is warmth — the invisible people of Hollowmere have quietly built a household around the hospice kitchen.

chapters.title: What the Dying Say
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. A new patient, Mr. Vance, counts not backwards but forwards, and begs Ivo to 'keep the tally broken.' He dies at dawn with a smile, and the bell rings thirteen times. The beat is grief laced with suspicion — Ivo wonders if breaking the count is mercy or catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Old Families
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Odile is sent to the Marchetti farm to ask questions and finds the last founding family keeping their own count: chalk marks on a barn wall, one per year since 1911. The beat is class dread — the founders' descendants know everything and have decided the harvest is simply the price of living in Hollowmere.

chapters.title: Thirteen Rings
chapters.summary: Tam, POV. After the thirteenth ring, Tam's cousin disappears — not dead, but unremembered; even his photographs have gone blank. The beat is horror of erasure — the bell doesn't kill, it subtracts, and only the invisible people notice who is missing.

chapters.title: Ritual, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. In the parish archive, Ivo and Brigid reconstruct the founders' ritual: a covenant renewed every generation by 'feeding the tally,' designed to keep something called the Quiet Tenant bound beneath the bell tower. The founders' line died out mid-ritual in 1911; the bell was melted to end the bargain. It didn't end. The beat is terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Tenant Below
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Odile descends into the tower's sealed undercroft and finds the melted bell's core, still warm, still ringing soundlessly against her bones. She hears it counting her. The beat is intimate terror — the Tenant isn't a monster in the dark; it's an accounting, patient and impersonal.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. The Marchettis offer a deal: finish the ritual, sacrifice the outsiders, and Hollowmere is safe for another century. Ivo's found family is the intended tally. The beat is moral fracture — Ivo, who has kept everyone alive by following rules, is offered the ultimate rule-following atrocity.

chapters.title: Doors, Counted
chapters.summary: Tam, POV. The village turns: doors that were open to Tam for years are shut, his wages left in envelopes like severance. The beat is betrayal — the found family realizes their invisibility was never protection, it was inventory.

chapters.title: Sister Brigid's Confession
chapters.summary: Brigid, POV. Brigid admits she came to Hollowmere fleeing her own scandal, and that the Church once ran the tally — her defrocking was for asking the same questions Ivo is asking now. The beat is grace — confession as solidarity, not absolution.

chapters.title: Forwards, Not Back
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Re-reading Vance's forwards count, Ivo realizes the dying weren't being taken — they were volunteering, paying down the tally to protect others. The beat is devastating tenderness — every patient Ivo comforted was a shield, and Ivo was the one they were shielding each other from.

chapters.title: The Tally Broken
chapters.summary: Odile and Tam, POV alternating. They sabotage the Marchetti barn wall, smearing the century of chalk marks, and the village's crops fail overnight — the covenant's collateral. The beat is defiance with a bill attached — breaking the ritual means the whole village pays, not just the invisible.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Counts Its Dead
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. The village erupts: the Marchettis demand a sacrifice, neighbors arm themselves, and the bell rings continuously now, audible in daylight. The beat is siege — justice outside the law means the found family must decide the village's fate without any court, church, or constable willing to help.

chapters.title: What Odile Heard Down There
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Odile reveals the Tenant spoke to her — it doesn't want blood, it wants a name freely given to hold the count, and it has been waiting since 1911 for someone to choose it. The beat is terrible hope — there is a third option between harvest and ruin, and it costs exactly one person everything.

chapters.title: The Volunteers
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Each member of the found family privately offers themselves; Ivo discovers their notes and realizes love has become a bidding war. The beat is heartbreak — the family Ivo built is trying to dismantle itself to save Ivo.

chapters.title: The Last Ring
chapters.summary: Climax, Ivo POV. At the tower, the Marchettis attempt a forced harvest; Brigid is gravely wounded holding them off, Tam breaks the undercroft seal, and Odile begins the ritual. The beat is chaos and courage — everything the family built is spent in one night.

chapters.title: A Name, Freely Given
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Before Odile can finish, Ivo speaks their own name into the bell's silence, taking the Tenant's place as the one who holds the count. The beat is sacrifice without melodrama — Ivo's compulsions were preparation all along; no one counts doors like a person becoming a door.

chapters.title: Silence, Kept
chapters.summary: Tam, POV. The bell stops mid-ring. The Marchetti chalk wall crumbles to dust; the undercroft is empty except for warm air and a faint, patient counting only Tam can still hear. The beat is hollow victory — the Tenant is bound, but bound to Ivo now, and Tam cannot stop listening for them.

chapters.title: The Hospice Without a Nurse
chapters.summary: Odile, POV, weeks later. The village remembers Ivo the way it remembered Tam's cousin — photographs blank, name on no ledger — but the found family keeps Ivo's rituals alive: lights on, doors counted, a place set at the table. The beat is mourning as inheritance — found family means the rituals outlive the person.

chapters.title: Counting Forwards
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Odile POV, then Ivo's voice in the last lines. At the hospice, the dying have stopped counting backwards; now they count forwards, smiling, toward someone holding the tally on the other side. The beat is bittersweet transcendence — justice was never the law or the ritual, but the choice of who pays, and Ivo chose. The last count is Ivo's: one, two, three — still keeping the doors.
